summary: Lookout of the Moshannon Forest District; a 2019 news report calls it brand new and 80 feet tall. No build date, access rule or current status found.

events.note: Described as brand new and first used in spring 2019. The article does not give the construction date.

sources.title: With new lookout towers, Pennsylvania goes old-school to detect wildfires

notes_for_editor: The only history source is one 2019 StateImpact article, which describes a new Chestnut Ridge tower used by the Moshannon Forest District. The OSM point (41.1632, -78.3559) is about 2 km from OSM's 'The Knobs Fire Tower' (41.1487, -78.3354). The article calls the Knobs a 98-year-old tower no longer in use and describes an older tower near the new one without naming it. Check whether the record point is the new tower or the old one before trusting the location. Pennsylvania's best-known Chestnut Ridge tower (Pondfield, Fayette County) is a different structure and was not used. No access, status or staffing record beyond 2019 was found.
